Assuming your installation is up-to-date with the github version, it looks like a Windows bug in rstan:::find_rtools and/or a configuration error. For some reason, the following code is returning either a 0-length vector or NULL:

system2(file.path(Sys.getenv("R_HOME"), "bin",
                  Sys.getenv("R_ARCH_BIN"), "R"),
                  args = "CMD config CXX", stdout = TRUE)

A good way to debug would be to execute (from the console, or ideally directly into the Rmd):

print(execPath <- file.path(Sys.getenv("R_HOME"), "bin", Sys.getenv("R_ARCH_BIN"), "R"))
print(CXX <- system2(execPath, args = "CMD config CXX", stdout = TRUE))

In my Windows R session R_ARCH_BIN isn't defined, but it looks like it maybe should refer to R_ARCH. A workaround would be to define those environment variables:

if (nchar(Sys.getenv("R_HOME")) == 0) Sys.setenv(R_HOME = R.home())
if (nchar(Sys.getenv("R_ARCH_BIN")) == 0) Sys.setenv(R_ARCH_BIN = .Platform$r_arch)

Presumably, an upstream fix is to check for the NULL result and instead find R by using file.path(R.home("bin"), "R").

On Thu, Nov 24, 2016 at 3:27 PM Vincent Dorie <vj...@nyu.edu> wrote:

R does not seem to exist where R thinks it does, so whether or not the C++ toolchain is installed correctly R cannot be queried to find it. The inline package performs a similar check (using system and R.home("bin") instead of system2 and environment variables) but directly has R compile the code using R CMD SHLIB. This possibly implies that it is only R CMD config that is failing. It is worth trying to execute from the windows command line "C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-33~1.1/bin/x64/R" and seeing if R opens in the console. If I recall, the various CMDs are implemented by links, so it is possible that only the config is missing.
